crime: One girl made {WITCH_NAME} collect other prisoners' belongings with her magic, then displayed them as her own collection by an upstairs window. At midday she ordered an embroidered handkerchief by Friday and turned away before {WITCH_NAME} could answer.

That evening, {WITCH_NAME} claimed a vial of heart medicine from the infirmary. Its keeper delivered it and left, half convinced she had meant to make the trip. A whole vial was enough to stop a healthy heart.

The next morning, {WITCH_NAME} claimed the girl's syrup jar, which the girl normally kept to herself. When it arrived at her cell door, she poured the medicine onto the thick syrup and put the jar back outside. The girl carried it away, confused about why she had brought it.

At midday, the girl stirred her usual spoonful from the top into tea and drank before the others. The medicine had stayed in a separate layer; that first spoon took almost all of it. Within an hour she was dead.
The keeper recognized the medicine's bitter smell in the syrup, and a vial was missing from the infirmary. The jar had left its owner's keeping just once that morning, at {WITCH_NAME}'s door.
fields.epitaph: She could claim anything, and still belonged to someone else's wants.
fields.epithet: A Queen Kept as Someone's Errand Girl
execution: A giant iron hand traveled on a track above a circle of empty chairs. It gripped her body, enclosing her hands, and carried her from chair to chair. Each time it set her down, it took a tighter grip to lift her again. At the last chair it kept closing until it crushed her.

magic.name: Requisition
magic.text: When she claims an object as hers, its owner is compelled to bring it to her.
